title: Pointwise versality gives Artinian lifting at every finite type field point
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning that cartesian pullbacks exist along every base morphism and each fibre is a groupoid. A local ring has a unique maximal ideal; an Artinian ring satisfies the descending chain condition on ideals. Assume the Rim-Schlessinger property: whenever $B'=B\amalg_A A'$ is a pushout of spectra of Artinian local rings of finite type over $R$ and $A\to A'$ is a closed immersion defined by a nilpotent ideal, restriction gives an equivalence $\mathcal X(B')\simeq\mathcal X(B)\times_{\mathcal X(A)}\mathcal X(A')$. Let $U$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $S$ and $x\in\mathcal X(U)$. A point $v$ of an $S$-scheme $V$ is a finite type point if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ is of finite type [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $V$ locally of finite type over $S$ and $y\in\mathcal X(V)$, say that $y$ is versal at a finite type point $v$ if, for every surjection $B'\to B$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with residue field identified with $\kappa(v)$, every $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$ restricting to the canonical point $v$, every $z\in\mathcal X(B')$, and every isomorphism $z|_B\cong a^*y$, there exist a lift $a':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to V$ of $a$ and an isomorphism $z\cong(a')^*y$ extending the prescribed isomorphism. Assume $x$ is versal at every finite type point of $U$. Then the following lifting property holds, including finite extensions of the residue field of the image point: For each field $l$ of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], each $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}l\to U$, each surjection $B'\to B$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras whose residue fields are identified with $l$, each $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$ restricting to $\alpha$, each $z\in\mathcal X(B')$, and each isomorphism $z|_B\cong a^*x$, there exist a lift $a':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to U$ of $a$ and an isomorphism $z\cong(a')^*x$ extending that isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix all data in the conclusion and put $u=\alpha(\operatorname{Spec}l)$ and $k=\kappa(u)$. On any affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U$ of $u$, a finite set of $R$-algebra generators of $l$ also generates $l$ as an $A$-algebra, since the image of $R$ lies in the image of $A$. Thus $\alpha$ is of finite type: it is locally of finite type and its source is a singleton. Apply the finite-type field-point characterization to obtain that $u$ is a finite type point and $[l:k]<\infty$. Since $k\subset l$ is an $R$-subalgebra and $l$ is finite as a $k$-module, Artin--Tate gives that $k$ is of finite type over $R$. The assumed versality of $x$ therefore applies at $u$.

source.place: Tag 07XT (lemma-versal-smooth), equation-smooth, and Tag 07XG (lemma-versal-change-of-field); versality is Tag 07XF (definition-versal).

proof.text: Form $C=B\times_l k$ and $C^\prime=B^\prime\times_l k$. The residue-restriction lemma gives Artinian local rings with residue field $k$ and a surjection $C^\prime\twoheadrightarrow C$. Its kernel identifies with $\ker(B^\prime\to B)$ and is nilpotent, being contained in the maximal ideal of $B^\prime$, which is nilpotent by the Artinian local structure lemma. The finite-type residue criterion shows that $B,B^\prime,C,C^\prime$ are of finite type over $R$; the same is true of $k$ and $l$ by step 1 and the original hypothesis. Thus every scheme in the two gluing squares below satisfies the finite-type hypothesis of (RS).

source.place: Tag 07XT (lemma-versal-smooth), equation-smooth, and Tag 07XG (lemma-versal-change-of-field); versality is Tag 07XF (definition-versal).

proof.text: The two squares with top row $\operatorname{Spec}l\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ (respectively $\operatorname{Spec}B^\prime$) and bottom row $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ (respectively $\operatorname{Spec}C^\prime$) are pushouts by the affine clause of the scheme pushout theorem. Its hypotheses hold: $B\to l$ and $B^\prime\to l$ are surjective, and $k\to l$ is integral, since the finitely many powers $1,t,\ldots,t^{[l:k]}$ are linearly dependent over $k$ for each $t\in l$, yielding a monic equation. The affine-neighbourhood condition is automatic because $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B^\prime$ are affine. The top closed immersions are nilpotent by step 2. Since $a$ and the canonical point $u:\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$ agree on $\operatorname{Spec}l$, the first pushout gives a map $a_C:\operatorname{Spec}C\to U$ with these restrictions.

source.place: Tag 07XT (lemma-versal-smooth), equation-smooth, and Tag 07XG (lemma-versal-change-of-field); versality is Tag 07XF (definition-versal).

proof.text: Write $x_u=u^*x$. Restrict the given isomorphism $\theta:z|_B\cong a^*x$ to $l$, obtaining $z|_l\cong x_u|_l$. Essential surjectivity of the assumed (RS) equivalence for the second square gives $w^\prime\in\mathcal X(C^\prime)$ with isomorphisms $w^\prime|_{B^\prime}\cong z$ and $w^\prime|_k\cong x_u$ compatible with this identification over $l$. On restricting to $C$, compose its $B$-component with $\theta$ and its $k$-component with the identity of $x_u$. These components agree over $l$ by construction. Full faithfulness of the (RS) equivalence for the first square produces an isomorphism $w^\prime|_C\cong a_C^*x$ with exactly those two components.

source.place: Tag 07XT (lemma-versal-smooth), equation-smooth, and Tag 07XG (lemma-versal-change-of-field); versality is Tag 07XF (definition-versal).

proof.text: Apply versality at $u$ to the surjection $C^\prime\to C$, the map $a_C$, the object $w^\prime$, and this prescribed isomorphism. It gives $a_{C^\prime}:\operatorname{Spec}C^\prime\to U$ lifting $a_C$ and an isomorphism $w^\prime\cong a_{C^\prime}^*x$ restricting to that prescribed isomorphism over $C$. Restrict along $\operatorname{Spec}B^\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}C^\prime$ and use $w^\prime|_{B^\prime}\cong z$. The result is $a^\prime:\operatorname{Spec}B^\prime\to U$ with $a^\prime|_B=a$ and $z\cong(a^\prime)^*x$. Its restriction to $B$ is exactly $\theta$ because the $B$-component in step 4 was chosen to be $\theta$.
